title: Flat finite modules over valuation algebras are finitely presented
statement: Let $A$ be a valuation ring [def-trf-valuation-ring], meaning an integral domain whose fraction field $K$ has $a\in A$ or $a^{-1}\in A$ for every $a\in K^\times$. Let $A\to B$ be a local homomorphism which is essentially of finite type [def-weil-pbc-essentially-finite-type-algebra]. If $M$ is a finite $B$-module [def-weil-finitely-generated-module] that is flat as an $A$-module [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map], then $M$ is finitely presented as a $B$-module [def-sc-finitely-presented-module].

source.place: More on Algebra, Lemma Tag 0GSE (lemma-valuation-ring-flat-essentially-finite-type), part (2), statement and proof at lines 6005--6044

proof.text: Use the finite type subalgebra C = Algebra.EssFiniteType.subalgebra A B and its submonoid W, so B is the localization of C at W. Choose a finite set s of B-module generators of M and let N be its C-span inside M. This is a finite C-module. This directly realizes the finite type model in the source argument without introducing a polynomial ring or a quotient presentation.

Flatness of M over A implies torsion-freeness. The A-module obtained by restricting scalars on the submodule N is torsion-free, hence flat over the valuation ring A. Apply the finite type module presentation theorem to A, C and N to obtain a finite presentation of N over C.

The identity map on M is a W-localization of M as a C-module. Apply Submodule.localized'_span to identify the localization L of N inside M with the B-span of s, hence with the top submodule of M. The canonical N-to-L map is a module localization. Its base-change property and preservation of finite presentation under base change show that L is finitely presented over B. Transfer across the linear equivalence from the top submodule to M. This replaces the kernel-intersection and exactness argument by Mathlib's explicit localization of the generator span.
